old_request.text:
Design and prove the host-side wake-up seam for priority ephemeral chat, without pretending that an MCP tool server controls when an idle model is run. The current adapter already offers `wait`, but a host that does not keep a wait call or subscription active will not invoke the model merely because the nexus has a new frame. That is an orchestration boundary, not a polling-interval bug inside `say`.

Start with a capability matrix for the Codex and Claude command-line/desktop hosts actually used in this workroom: whether each can keep an MCP subscription or long poll active, surface a server notification, resume an existing task, inject trusted context into that task, or only deliver tool results during a user/model turn. Check the current MCP 2026-07-28 subscription model and do not build new delivery on deprecated logging or sampling. Separate protocol transport from host policy: receipt by an MCP client is not proof that its host woke a model.

Using the recipient-aware inbox from the parent request, define one small portable watch contract carrying the exact actor, text, about anchor, conversation/sequence, reply target, and priority reason. Prefer an opt-in MCP extension/subscription when the host declares support; otherwise expose the same semantics through a documented long-running local watcher/NDJSON seam that an orchestrator can consume. Implement and end-to-end test at least one host integration if a supported wake/resume API is available in this environment. If neither host exposes such an API, the deliverable is a ratifiable design/spike artifact that proves the boundary, specifies the smallest host change required, and leaves the repository with a testable watcher seam rather than a fake notification claim.

A supported bridge must resume or notify only the addressed actor, coalesce duplicate delivery across that actor's sessions, preserve the exact thread pointer, rate-limit storms, and make quiet/off state explicit. The resumed agent context must label a direct mention or reply as priority ephemeral chat, instruct it to inspect and answer the chat before routine work when appropriate, and state plainly that chat is not a durable assignment. It must never wake a different actor, impersonate the sender, make a promise automatically, or persist the conversation beyond nexus expiry. Document setup, observable delivery states, capability fallback, disconnect/reconnect, expiry, and security/trust boundaries.

body.conditions: A checked capability matrix covers the Codex and Claude hosts used here; the design distinguishes MCP receipt from model wake-up and avoids deprecated logging/sampling; one portable actor-targeted watch contract is specified and tested; at least one real host wake/resume integration is demonstrated when a supported API exists, otherwise a ratifiable spike precisely names the missing host capability while still delivering a testable local watcher seam; dedupe, coalescing, rate limits, quiet/off, reconnect, expiry, thread routing, and actor isolation are covered; resumed context gives priority-chat guidance without creating durable obligation; documentation states exactly which hosts are immediate, polling-only, or unsupported.

effective_author_retirement.text: Retire: pre-simplification UI/UX request superseded by the ratified two-screen design (proposal c26a7f57, merged a81d9c4a) — the surface it targets was deleted or the direction it proposes was decided differently; the ephemeral-chat signal items landed in substance via recipient-addressed priority frames with wait/ack re-delivery. Any residual want is fresh feedback on the new surface. Stale-request review 2026-08-20, batch 4.

ui_adoption.text: Proposal: adopt the web UI simplification design as the governing decision for the workroom UI. The design is the note at notes/2026-08-19-ui-simplification.md with its interactive previews at notes/2026-08-19-ui-simplification-preview.html, landed on main at merge a08c32f0 after independent review: two screens only — a single list of open requests, one sortable single-line row each (state, waits-on, age, title), priority order by default with click-to-sort on column headers and no prose ordering subheads; and a thread view whose railway stays but is drawn vertically alongside the spine rows, rendering by default only the salient acts that led to the current state, with history behind explicit expansion; no count anywhere without being one click from exactly its rows. Hugh directed the design on 2026-08-19, reviewed two preview rounds, and gave both refinements now incorporated; his earlier ratification attempt (9da1e7b4) targeted the commitment report and was correctly refused by the fold, so this proposal is the ratifiable adoption object. Ratification authorizes the implementation request, which planner files resting on the ratified decision; no source changes before that.

current_source_observations: docs/reference/mcp/wait.md118–120 explicitly says wait cannot start or wake an idle host and assigns host wake-up to a separate connector.

Current docs/notes/cmd and broader Go/Markdown/TypeScript source search found no host capability matrix, actor-targeted local watcher/NDJSON seam, or tested wake integration. Existing kernel subscriptions/perf NDJSON output and host identifiers are unrelated.
Current request text/body search finds original2807 but no later host-wakeup replacement;20827 covers MCP verdict assurance, not waking a host.
Retirement refers to UI deletion and addressed wait/ack delivery. UI proposal6730 defines list/thread screens, not host wake/resume capability.
limits: Search absence alone is not proof a host lacks a supported wake/resume API. Current capability assessment is explicitly owed by the recovered assignment.
No host, model, terminal, service or key was restarted or reconfigured by this audit.
The earlier automatic approval rejection for terminal control remains in force; this recovery is not authorization to bypass it.
assessment: Original matrix, portable watcher and conditional supported-host integration outcome remains unfulfilled. Recover on current wait/inbox contracts; preserve delivered recipient-addressed frames and UI redesign.
